proofs.proof_tex:
By \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\), the three matrices \(H_j\) are positive definite, so every square root and inverse used below exists.  Put
\[
 U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}.
\]
The first covariance equation in \(\text{def:raw-fiber}\) is equivalent to
\[
 UU^{\mathsf T}
 =H_1^{-1/2}WH_0W^{\mathsf T}H_1^{-1/2}=I_p.
\]
Since \(U\) is square, this says exactly that \(U\in O(p)\), and the inverse change of variables is \(W=H_1^{1/2}UH_0^{-1/2}\).  Under this change of variables, the second covariance equation is
\[
 H_1^{1/2}URU^{\mathsf T}H_1^{1/2}=H_2,
 \qquad\text{or equivalently}\qquad URU^{\mathsf T}=S.
\]
Thus \(SU=UR\).  Because \(R\) and \(S\) are real symmetric positive-definite matrices, an orthogonal intertwiner exists only if their eigenvalues, including multiplicities, agree.  If they agree, their spectral resolutions give
\[
 U=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}Q_\lambda O_\lambda P_\lambda^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad O_\lambda\in O(m_\lambda),
\]
and this representation is unique relative to the fixed orthonormal frames \(P_\lambda,Q_\lambda\): indeed, \(SU=UR\) maps the \(\lambda\)-eigenspace of \(R\) into the \(\lambda\)-eigenspace of \(S\), and \(O_\lambda=Q_\lambda^{\mathsf T}UP_\lambda\).

The two mean equations become, after multiplication by \(H_1^{-1/2}\),
\[
 U H_0^{-1/2}[d_0,d_1]=H_1^{-1/2}[d_1,d_2].
\]
Projecting this equality onto the \(\lambda\)-eigenspace of \(S\) gives precisely
\[
 O_\lambda A_\lambda=B_\lambda.
\]
Necessity of the block Gram condition follows from orthogonality:
\[
 B_\lambda^{\mathsf T}B_\lambda
 =A_\lambda^{\mathsf T}O_\lambda^{\mathsf T}O_\lambda A_\lambda
 =A_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_\lambda.
\]

Conversely, suppose the spectra match and the displayed Gram equality holds in every block.  For a fixed \(\lambda\), define on \(\operatorname{ran}(A_\lambda)\)
\[
 L_\lambda(A_\lambda c)=B_\lambda c,
 \qquad c\in\mathbb R^2.
\]
This is well defined: if \(A_\lambda c=0\), then
\[
 \lVert B_\lambda c\rVert^2
 =c^{\mathsf T}B_\lambda^{\mathsf T}B_\lambda c
 =c^{\mathsf T}A_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_\lambda c=0.
\]
The same Gram identity shows that \(L_\lambda\) preserves all inner products and maps onto \(\operatorname{ran}(B_\lambda)\).  In particular the two ranges have the common dimension \(r_\lambda\).  Choose orthonormal frames \(F_A,F_B\) for these ranges and frames \(N_A,N_B\) for their orthogonal complements, arranging \(F_B^{\mathsf T}L_\lambda F_A=I_{r_\lambda}\).  Every orthogonal extension, and no other one, is
\[
 O_\lambda=F_BF_A^{\mathsf T}+N_B Z_\lambda N_A^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad Z_\lambda\in O(k_\lambda).
\]
It satisfies \(O_\lambda A_\lambda=B_\lambda\).  Hence the choices form a torsor for \(O(k_\lambda)\), including the conventions that \(O(0)\) is trivial and \(O(1)=\{-1,1\}\).  Since \(\dim O(k)=k(k-1)/2\), substitution into the inverse whitening map yields exactly, without repetition,
\[
 W=H_1^{1/2}\left(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}Q_\lambda O_\lambda P_\lambda^{\mathsf T}\right)H_0^{-1/2}.
\]
This proves both directions of the certificate and the asserted fiber dimensions.

Identify a matrix \(U\) with \(u=\operatorname{vec}(U)\), write \(f(u;\zeta)=F_{\mathrm{res}}(U;\zeta)\), and let
\[
 Q(u;\zeta)=\frac12\lVert f(u;\zeta)\rVert_2^2,
 \qquad
 \Psi(u;\zeta)=D_uf(u;\zeta)^{\mathsf T}f(u;\zeta).
\]
At the fixed exact branch \((w,z)\), \(f(w;z)=0\).  Therefore
\[
 D_u\Psi(w;z)=D_uf(w;z)^{\mathsf T}D_uf(w;z).
\]
The hypothesis \(\gamma_W>0\) makes this matrix positive definite, with smallest eigenvalue \(\gamma_W^2\).  Set \(A_0=[D_u\Psi(w;z)]^{-1}\) and \(\Phi_\zeta(u)=u-A_0\Psi(u;\zeta)\).  Its derivative in \(u\) is zero at \((w,z)\).  Continuity therefore supplies neighborhoods on which \(\Phi_\zeta\) is a contraction and maps a closed ball about \(w\) into itself.  Iteration is Cauchy at a geometric rate, so it has a unique fixed point \(u(\zeta)\) there; this fixed point is the unique local stationary point.  Continuity of the Hessian keeps it positive definite, so the point is the unique local minimizer.  At the population moment \(z\), compactness of the fixed isolating ball and the absence of any other raw root imply that the residual norm is bounded away from zero outside every sufficiently small neighborhood of \(w\).  Uniform continuity in \(\zeta\) then forces the minimizer over that ball to lie in the contraction neighborhood for all \(\zeta\) sufficiently close to \(z\).  Thus it is exactly the branch-local estimator \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) from \(\text{def:local-branch-estimator}\).  Subtracting the two fixed-point equations and applying a first-order Taylor expansion proves differentiability, and repeated differentiation proves smoothness.  Its first derivative is
\[
 Du(z)[a]=-\bigl(D_WF^{\mathsf T}D_WF\bigr)^{-1}
 D_WF^{\mathsf T}D_zF[a].
\]
The isolating-ball hypothesis therefore selects this branch and excludes every other population root from the local construction.

Strict stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, covariance-positivity, and equilibrium margins make every operation in \(\theta(U,\zeta)\) smooth near \((W,z)\).  In particular, the Stein derivative is obtained by solving an invertible linear equation, the logarithm derivative by its resolvent integral, and the equilibrium derivative by differentiating an inverse.  The composite branch map
\[
 g(\zeta)=\theta(U(\zeta),\zeta)
\]
is therefore smooth, and its derivative at \(z\) is exactly \(J_\theta\).

It remains to establish the moment limit used by the theorem.  For one snapshot, write \(Y=m+Z\) with \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,C)\), and define the centered single-observation moment vector
\[
 \xi=\bigl(Z,\operatorname{vech}(ZZ^{\mathsf T}-C)\bigr).
\]
It has finite moments of every order.  Differentiating the Gaussian moment-generating function \(\exp(t^{\mathsf T}Ct/2)\) shows
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_iZ_jZ_\ell]=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(Z_iZ_j,Z_rZ_s)=C_{ir}C_{js}+C_{is}C_{jr}.
\]
Thus the mean and covariance blocks of \(\operatorname{Cov}(\xi)\) have zero cross-covariance.  More explicitly, if \(L_p\) is the elimination matrix satisfying \(\operatorname{vech}(A)=L_p\operatorname{vec}(A)\) for symmetric \(A\), and \(\mathsf K_p\operatorname{vec}(A)=\operatorname{vec}(A^{\mathsf T})\), then the contribution of snapshot \(k\) in snapshot-interlaced coordinates is
\[
 \Omega_k=\frac1{\pi_k}\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
 C_k,\ L_p(I_{p^2}+\mathsf K_p)(C_k\otimes C_k)L_p^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]
Let \(\mathsf P\) be the fixed permutation taking the snapshot-interlaced stack to the declared order \(z=(m_0,\ldots,m_3,\operatorname{vech}C_0,\ldots,\operatorname{vech}C_3)\).  Then
\[
 \Omega=\mathsf P\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_0,\Omega_1,\Omega_2,\Omega_3)\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The usual sample covariance differs from the average of \(ZZ^{\mathsf T}\) by the outer product of the sample-mean error and, if the divisor is \(n-1\), an asymptotically negligible factor; this difference is \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1})\).

For completeness, the finite-dimensional Gaussian limit follows from the characteristic function calculation
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left(i t^{\mathsf T}\xi/\sqrt n\right)
 =1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Cov}(\xi)t}{2n}+o(n^{-1}),
\]
whose \(n\)-th power tends to \(\exp[-t^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Cov}(\xi)t/2]\).  By \(\text{ass:unpaired-sampling}\), the samples at distinct snapshot labels are independent.  Applying the calculation at each snapshot and using \(n_k/N\to\pi_k\in(0,1)\) from \(\text{ass:sample-shares}\) gives
\[
 \sqrt N(\widehat z-z)\Longrightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Omega).
\]
The blocks from different snapshot labels are independent; all correlations created later by forming \(H_j,d_j\) are retained because these differences are fixed linear transformations of the full vector \(z\).

Taylor expansion of the smooth map \(g\) gives
\[
 \sqrt N\{g(\widehat z)-g(z)\}
 =J_\theta\sqrt N(\widehat z-z)+o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\]
and substitution of the preceding characteristic-function limit proves
\[
 \sqrt N\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}-\theta(W,z)\bigr)
 \Longrightarrow\mathcal N(0,J_\theta\Omega J_\theta^{\mathsf T}).
\]
In particular the last coordinate is \(\widehat\mu_0=\widehat m_0\).  The empirical covariances converge to \(C_k\), the deterministic shares converge to \(\pi_k\), and the smooth local solution converges to \(W\).  The explicit Gaussian fourth-moment formula above and continuity of all derivatives therefore imply that replacing \((z,W,\Omega,J_\theta)\) by their empirical plug-in counterparts converges in probability to \(J_\theta\Omega J_\theta^{\mathsf T}\).  This establishes consistent covariance estimation separately on every specified regular branch, without requiring empirical spectral or Gram equalities.

By \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\), a nonempty raw fiber is a product, over \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), of torsors for \(O(k_\lambda)\).  The group \(O(0)\) is a singleton, \(O(1)=\{-1,1\}\), and \(O(k)\) has local dimension \(k(k-1)/2>0\) when \(k\geq2\).  Hence the raw fiber is finite exactly when every \(k_\lambda\leq1\), and then
\[
 \#\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}
 =\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\#O(k_\lambda)
 =2^{\#\{\lambda:k_\lambda=1\}}=2^q.
\]
If some \(k_\lambda\geq2\), the product torsor has positive local dimension at every point.  The three admissibility requirements in \(\text{def:admissible-fiber}\) are strict and relatively open on this torsor.  Indeed, spectral radius is continuous; avoidance of \(( -\infty,0]\) persists when the roots of the characteristic polynomial are perturbed sufficiently little; and, on \(\rho(W)<1\),
\[
 \operatorname{vec}(T_W)
 =\bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)^{-1}\operatorname{vec}(H_0)
\]
is continuous, so \(C_0-T_W\succ0\) is open.  Thus every admissible candidate on such a stratum lies in a positive-dimensional relatively open fiber.

We next prove the universal finite-fiber upper bound.  Suppose first that \(q\geq1\), and fix a block \(\lambda_0\) with \(k_{\lambda_0}=1\).  In the parameterization of \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\), changing only the sign of the one-dimensional residual isometry in that block defines a fixed-point-free involution of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\).  In orthonormal bases adapted to the probe span and its residual complement, this operation multiplies \(\det(O_{\lambda_0})\), and therefore \(\det(W)\), by \(-1\).  The \(2^q\) raw candidates consequently split into \(2^{q-1}\) matrices of each determinant sign.

Every raw candidate is invertible, because \(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1\) and \(H_0,H_1\succ0\).  If a real invertible matrix \(W\) satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing,
\]
then all of its real eigenvalues are positive, while each nonreal conjugate pair \(z,\overline z\) contributes \(z\overline z=|z|^2>0\) to the determinant.  Hence \(\det(W)>0\).  The logarithm-cut filter therefore rejects every negative-determinant raw candidate, so
\[
 \#\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\leq 2^{q-1}\qquad(q\geq1).
\]
If \(q=0\), the raw fiber itself has one member.  Finally,
\[
 q\leq\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}k_\lambda
 \leq\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}m_\lambda=p.
\]
Together with \(p\geq2\) from \(\text{ass:dimension}\), this gives \(\#\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\leq2^{p-1}\) on every finite stratum, including the case \(q=0\).  By the bijection in \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\), the same bound holds for compatible structural explanations.

It remains to attain the bound while satisfying all strict filters.  Let \(Q_\circ\) be the cyclic permutation matrix defined by
\[
 Q_\circ e_i=e_{i+1}\quad(1\leq i<p),
 \qquad Q_\circ e_p=e_1.
\]
Thus \(Q_\circ\in O(p)\) and \(\det(Q_\circ)=(-1)^{p-1}\).  For a sign matrix
\[
 D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_p),
 \qquad s_i\in\{-1,1\},
\]
one has
\[
 (Q_\circ D)^p=\left(\prod_{i=1}^p s_i\right)I_p.
\]
If \(\det(Q_\circ D)>0\), then \(\prod_i s_i=(-1)^{p-1}\).  Were \(-1\) an eigenvalue of \(Q_\circ D\), applying the preceding power identity to a corresponding nonzero eigenvector would give
\[
 (-1)^p=\prod_{i=1}^p s_i=(-1)^{p-1},
\]
a contradiction.  Because a real eigenvalue of an orthogonal matrix is either \(-1\) or \(1\), every orientation-preserving \(Q_\circ D\) avoids the negative real axis.

Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  At \(A_0=\alpha I_p\), each matrix \(A_0Q_\circ D\) with \(\det(Q_\circ D)>0\) is stable and avoids \(( -\infty,0]\).  This cut avoidance persists simultaneously for all such \(D\) when a positive diagonal matrix \(A\) is sufficiently close to \(A_0\).  To verify this without a spectral-gap assumption, suppose the contrary for one fixed \(D\).  There would be positive diagonal matrices \(A_n\to A_0\), numbers \(t_n\geq0\), and
\[
 \det(t_nI_p+A_nQ_\circ D)=0.
\]
For all large \(n\), \(\lVert A_n\rVert_2\leq c\) for some \(c<1\).  Since \(-t_n\) is then an eigenvalue of \(A_nQ_\circ D\), \(0\leq t_n\leq c\).  A subsequence has \(t_n\to t\in[0,c]\), and continuity of the determinant would imply
\[
 \det(tI_p+\alpha Q_\circ D)=0,
\]
contradicting the established cut avoidance at \(A_0\).  There are only \(2^{p-1}\) positive-orientation sign matrices, so one neighborhood works for all of them.  Choose within that neighborhood
\[
 A=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_p),
 \qquad 0<\alpha_i<1,
 \qquad \alpha_i^2\neq\alpha_j^2\quad(i\neq j).
\]
For every sign matrix \(D\),
\[
 \lVert AQ_\circ D\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2
 =\max_i\alpha_i<1,
\]
so every raw candidate below is stable; by the choice of \(A\), every positive-determinant one also passes the logarithm-cut filter.

Define zero mean differences and the three covariance differences by
\[
 d_0=d_1=d_2=0,
 \qquad H_0=I_p,
 \qquad H_1=A^2,
 \qquad H_2=AQ_\circ A^2Q_\circ^{\mathsf T}A.
\]
All three \(H_j\) are positive definite, so \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\) holds.  Moreover
\[
 R=A^2,
 \qquad S=Q_\circ A^2Q_\circ^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The squared diagonal entries of \(A\) are distinct, so the common spectral blocks are one dimensional, with source eigenvectors \(e_i\) and target eigenvectors \(Q_\circ e_i\).  Both probe matrices in every block vanish because all \(d_j\) vanish.  Hence
\[
 m_\lambda=1,\qquad r_\lambda=0,\qquad k_\lambda=1,\qquad q=p.
\]
The block parameterization in \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\) now gives, exactly once each, the \(2^p\) raw matrices
\[
 W_D=AQ_\circ D,
 \qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_p),
 \qquad s_i\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Directly, their defining equations are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 W_DH_0W_D^{\mathsf T}&=A^2=H_1,\\
 W_DH_1W_D^{\mathsf T}
 &=AQ_\circ DA^2DQ_\circ^{\mathsf T}A
 =AQ_\circ A^2Q_\circ^{\mathsf T}A=H_2,
 \end{aligned}
\]
where \(DA^2D=A^2\); the mean equations hold because the probes are zero.

It remains to realize these differences as positive-definite Gaussian level covariances and to make the reconstructed measurement covariance positive on every branch.  For each of the finitely many sign matrices define
\[
 T_D=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}W_D^j(W_D^{\mathsf T})^j.
\]
The bound \(\lVert W_D\rVert_2<1\) makes this series converge, its zeroth term gives \(T_D\succ0\), and shifting the series proves
\[
 T_D-W_DT_DW_D^{\mathsf T}=I_p=H_0.
\]
Let
\[
 b=1+\lambda_{\max}(H_0+H_1+H_2)
\]
and choose
\[
 c>\max\left\{b,\max_D\lambda_{\max}(T_D)\right\}.
\]
Set
\[
 C_0=cI_p,
 \qquad C_1=C_0-H_0,
 \qquad C_2=C_1-H_1,
 \qquad C_3=C_2-H_2,
 \qquad m_0=m_1=m_2=m_3=0.
\]
The choice \(c>b\) makes every \(C_k\) positive definite.  For each \(D\), put \(E_D=C_0-T_D\).  The choice of \(c\) gives \(E_D\succ0\).  Using the Stein equation and the two raw congruences successively yields, for \(k=0,1,2,3\),
\[
 C_k=W_D^kT_D(W_D^{\mathsf T})^k+E_D\succ0.
\]
Thus the displayed \(C_k\) are well-defined positive-definite observed covariance matrices, their adjacent differences are exactly the prescribed strict positive-definite \(H_j\), and \(E_D\) is a common positive-definite measurement covariance across the four snapshots within each explanation.

Because \(\det(A)>0\), exactly half of the sign matrices satisfy
\[
 \det(W_D)=\det(A)\det(Q_\circ D)>0.
\]
All of these \(2^{p-1}\) candidates pass stability, the logarithm cut, and \(E_D\succ0\), so they belong to \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  Every remaining candidate has negative determinant and therefore has a negative real eigenvalue by the conjugate-pair determinant argument above; it fails the logarithm-cut filter.  Hence
\[
 \#\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}=2^{p-1}.
\]
Finally, \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) reconstructs from every surviving \(W_D\) a unique real Hurwitz generator in the principal-log alias strip, the covariance \(T_D\), the positive common measurement covariance \(E_D\), the equilibrium \(x_D^\star=0\), and the initial mean \(\mu_0=0\).  Its bijection proves that these are exactly \(2^{p-1}\) distinct compatible structural explanations.  This proves attainability and completes the sharp classification.

Let \(A\) be a perturbation of a compatible transition \(W\).  Differentiating the four components of \(F_{\mathrm{res}}\) at the exact moment vector gives
\[
 D_WF[A]=\bigl(\operatorname{vech}(AH_0W^{\mathsf T}+WH_0A^{\mathsf T}),
 \operatorname{vech}(AH_1W^{\mathsf T}+WH_1A^{\mathsf T}),Ad_0,Ad_1\bigr).
\]
Put
\[
 U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}\in O(p),
 \qquad
 Z=H_1^{-1/2}AH_0^{1/2}.
\]
The first linearized covariance equation is \(ZU^{\mathsf T}+UZ^{\mathsf T}=0\).  Thus \(Z=UJ\) for a unique skew-symmetric matrix \(J\).  Substitution in the second equation, using \(H_1=H_0^{1/2}RH_0^{1/2}\), gives
\[
 JR+RJ^{\mathsf T}=0,
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad JR=RJ.
\]
The two mean equations are equivalent to
\[
 JH_0^{-1/2}d_0=0,
 \qquad
 JH_0^{-1/2}d_1=0.
\]
Because \(R\) is symmetric, \(JR=RJ\) makes \(J\) block diagonal in its eigenspaces.  In the \(\lambda\)-block, the last two equations say precisely that the skew-symmetric block \(J_\lambda\) annihilates \(\operatorname{ran}(A_\lambda)\), an \(r_\lambda\)-dimensional subspace.  Relative to that subspace and its orthogonal complement,
\[
 J_\lambda=0_{r_\lambda}\oplus \widetilde J_\lambda,
 \qquad
 \widetilde J_\lambda^{\mathsf T}=-\widetilde J_\lambda,
 \qquad
 \widetilde J_\lambda\in\mathbb R^{k_\lambda\times k_\lambda}.
\]
All changes of variables above are invertible.  Since the space of skew-symmetric \(k\)-by-\(k\) matrices has dimension \(k(k-1)/2\),
\[
 \dim\ker(D_WF)=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\frac{k_\lambda(k_\lambda-1)}2.
\]

Now consider the full structural coordinates \((W,T,E,x^\star,\mu_0)\) and the map from them to the four Gaussian means and covariances.  If their moment derivative vanishes, then the derivatives of all \(H_j,d_j\) vanish, so its \(W\)-component belongs to the kernel just computed.  Conversely, fix \(A\in\ker(D_WF)\).  The derivative \(\dot T\) required to keep \(H_0=T-WTW^{\mathsf T}\) fixed is uniquely determined by
\[
 \dot T-W\dot TW^{\mathsf T}=ATW^{\mathsf T}+WTA^{\mathsf T},
\]
because the stable Stein operator is invertible.  Keeping \(C_0=T+E\) fixed then uniquely forces \(\dot E=-\dot T\).  Keeping \(m_0=\mu_0\) fixed forces \(\dot\mu_0=0\), and keeping
\[
 m_1=W\mu_0+(I_p-W)x^\star
\]
fixed uniquely forces
\[
 \dot x^\star=-(I_p-W)^{-1}A(\mu_0-x^\star).
\]
The relations \(Ad_0=Ad_1=0\) then keep \(m_2,m_3\) fixed, and the two linearized congruences keep \(C_2,C_3\) fixed.  Hence projection onto the \(W\)-coordinate is a linear bijection between the kernel of the full moment derivative and \(\ker(D_WF)\).  Replacing \(W\) by its principal-logarithm coordinate \(G_W\) is a local smooth bijection and does not alter this nullity.

Finally, for one Gaussian marginal with positive-definite covariance \(C\), a mean perturbation \(u\) and symmetric covariance perturbation \(A_C\) have Fisher quadratic form
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}u+
 \frac12\operatorname{tr}(C^{-1}A_CC^{-1}A_C).
\]
This follows by differentiating the Gaussian log density and evaluating its second moments; after writing \(A_C=C^{1/2}BC^{1/2}\), the second term is \(\frac12\operatorname{tr}(B^2)\geq0\), with equality only for \(A_C=0\), while the first term vanishes only for \(u=0\).  By \(\text{ass:unpaired-sampling}\), the destructive-snapshot experiment draws independent samples separately from the four marginal laws.  Its Fisher quadratic form is therefore the positive weighted sum of the four marginal forms, and its kernel is exactly the kernel of the full parameter-to-moment derivative.  Thus the Fisher-information nullity equals
\[
 \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\frac{k_\lambda(k_\lambda-1)}2.
\]
It is zero exactly when every \(k_\lambda\leq1\), which is exactly the finite-raw-stratum condition given by the product of orthogonal completion fibers in \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\).

prose_updates.related_work: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 provides the closest congruence architecture. Its published class allows known process covariance \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time dynamics, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws. After a supplied measurement covariance \(E\) is subtracted, the model studied here is only its stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, \(Q=0\) subclass; the inherited consequence used here is the consecutive latent-covariance congruence, not equality of model classes or an exact reduction to every part of their theorem. It does not provide the present two-probe residual-rank classification or the sharp \(2^{p-1}\) admissible finite-fiber maximum. WangEtAl2024 proves a three-time-point result for deterministic affine dynamics from supplied state moments and motivates the \(\texttt{covar\_lin\_dyn}\) consumer. QWENDY2025 uses four supplied covariance matrices and simple spectra to resolve a homogeneous congruence problem, but it contains neither an unknown common additive covariance nor the exact three-snapshot norm and stabilizer classification proved here. MorimotoKashima2025 and InoueEtAl2026 estimate stochastic linear dynamics from direct snapshot marginals by Schrödinger-bridge optimization without a global common-noise identification certificate. Blevins2017 analyzes continuous-time aliases and motivates the principal-logarithm strip after the transition is recovered. KoltchinskiiLounici2017 supplies spectral perturbation tools, while HauensteinSottile2012 supplies root certificates; neither solves basis-invariant finite-branch enumeration with matrix-inequality filters. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 and Drton2009 locate set inference and singular asymptotics around the regular-stratum results. KongEtAl2023 studies process and measurement covariance identification from a paired stationary time series with known system matrices, a different information regime from destructive marginal snapshots.

proofs.proof_tex:
The exact three-snapshot compatibility certificate, torsor classification, local dimensions, zero-displacement elbow, and supermodel transfer are established by \(\text{thm:three-snapshot-exact-classification}\).  In particular, if \(d_0\ne0\), then \(r=1\) and every local admissible branch has dimension
\[
 \frac{(p-1)(p-2)}2,
\]
which is positive for \(p\ge3\).  At a true structural explanation, \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\) gives
\[
 d_0=(V-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star).
\]
By \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) and \(\text{ass:spacing}\), \(\rho(V)<1\), so \(I_p-V\) is invertible.  Hence \(d_0=0\) is exactly the proper affine locus \(\mu_0=x^\star\); its complement is open and dense in the mean parameter.  This proves the generic three-snapshot assertion.

We prove the four-snapshot assertion directly from the observable equations.  By \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\), \(H_0,H_1,H_2\) are positive definite and therefore invertible.  If \(W\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\), then \(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1\succ0\) implies \(\operatorname{rank}(W)=p\), so \(W\) is invertible.  Using the two covariance congruences in \(\text{def:raw-fiber}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M_1W
 &=H_2H_1^{-1}W\\
 &=(WH_1W^{\mathsf T})(WH_0W^{\mathsf T})^{-1}W\\
 &=WH_1W^{\mathsf T}W^{-\mathsf T}H_0^{-1}W^{-1}W\\
 &=WH_1H_0^{-1}=WM_0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first mean equation in \(\text{def:raw-fiber}\) is \(d_1=Wd_0\).  The intertwining identity therefore gives, by induction on \(j\),
\[
 M_1^jd_1=M_1^jWd_0=WM_0^jd_0
 \qquad(0\le j<p).
\]
Taking these vectors as columns yields
\[
 K_1=WK_0.
\]
Consequently, on the cyclic chart \(\det K_0\ne0\), every raw candidate is the observable rational functional
\[
 W=K_1K_0^{-1}=\mathcal K((m_k),(C_k)).
\]
In particular, the structural transition satisfies \(V=K_1K_0^{-1}\), and there is at most one raw, hence at most one admissible, transition.  This proves equality between the causal target and the observable recovery map rather than defining the target by that map.

It remains to prove that the cyclic chart is generic.  Choose pairwise distinct numbers \(v_i\in(0,1)\), and set
\[
 V=\operatorname{diag}(v_1,\ldots,v_p),\qquad
 G=h^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\log v_1,\ldots,\log v_p),\qquad
 \Sigma=I_p,\qquad E=I_p.
\]
Choose \(u=\mu_0-x^\star\) with every coordinate nonzero.  The generator is real, Hurwitz, and in the principal alias strip, while \(V=\exp(hG)\).  The latent covariance at snapshot \(j\) is \(\operatorname{diag}(v_i^{2j})\), so common-noise cancellation gives
\[
 H_j=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(v_i^{2j}(1-v_i^2)\bigr)\succ0
 \qquad(j=0,1,2),
\]
and
\[
 M_0=H_1H_0^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(v_1^2,\ldots,v_p^2).
\]
The affine mean recursion gives \(d_0=(V-I_p)u\), whose coordinates are all nonzero.  The \(i\)-th row of \(K_0\) is
\[
 d_{0i}(1,v_i^2,\ldots,v_i^{2(p-1)}).
\]
Subtracting successive columns in the usual determinant recursion for this Vandermonde matrix gives
\[
 \det K_0
 =\left(\prod_{i=1}^p d_{0i}\right)
 \prod_{1\le i<j\le p}(v_j^2-v_i^2)\ne0.
\]
The example has \(E=I_p\succ0\), so it lies in the strict admissible parameter domain.

Parameterize that domain by the transition coordinates \((V,\Sigma,E,x^\star,\mu_0)\).  The entries of \(H_j\) and \(d_j\) are polynomial in these coordinates, whereas the entries of \(M_0=H_1H_0^{-1}\) are rational with denominator a power of \(\det H_0\).  Thus \(\det K_0\) is rational on \(\det H_0\ne0\).  Clearing the denominator gives a polynomial numerator.  The preceding admissible example makes this numerator nonzero, so it is not the zero polynomial.  Its zero set is therefore a proper algebraic subset.  For completeness, the zero set of a nonzero real polynomial has empty interior and Lebesgue measure zero: induction on the number of coordinates reduces the assertion to the finite-root property of a nonzero univariate polynomial outside the common zero set of its coefficient polynomials.  Hence \(\det K_0\ne0\) outside a proper algebraic subset of the admissible transition-coordinate domain.

On this complement, the rational map recovers the sole raw candidate.  If that candidate passes the stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, and recovered-noise positivity filters in \(\text{def:admissible-fiber}\), then \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is its singleton.  The bijection in \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) then identifies \(G\), the latent initial covariance, the common measurement covariance, the equilibrium, and \(\mu_0=m_0\).  If the candidate fails a filter, there is no admissible explanation.  This proves the four-snapshot generic-identification claim.

Use operator norm for ordinary matrices and the Frobenius-induced operator norm for linear maps on \(\mathbb S^p\).  Write a hat for a perturbed quantity and \(\Delta A=\widehat A-A\).  The coordinatewise perturbation hypothesis gives
\[
 \lVert\Delta H_j\rVert\le2\epsilon,
 \qquad
 \lVert\Delta d_j\rVert\le2\epsilon.
\]
If \(\epsilon\le a_0/4\), then for every unit vector \(u\) and \(i\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}\widehat H_i u
 \ge u^{\mathsf T}H_i u-\lVert\Delta H_i\rVert
 \ge a_0-2\epsilon\ge a_0/2.
\]
Thus \(\widehat H_i\) is invertible and
\[
 \lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert\le\frac2{a_0}.
\]
The identity \(\widehat H_i^{-1}-H_i^{-1}=-\widehat H_i^{-1}(\Delta H_i)H_i^{-1}\), together with the definition of \(B_{\mathrm{norm}}\), yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat M_i-M_i\rVert
 &\le \lVert\Delta H_{i+1}\rVert\lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert
 +\lVert H_{i+1}\rVert\lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert
   \lVert\Delta H_i\rVert\lVert H_i^{-1}\rVert\\
 &\le\left(\frac4{a_0}+\frac{4B_{\mathrm{norm}}}{a_0^2}\right)\epsilon
 =c_M\epsilon,
 \qquad i\in\{0,1\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
When also \(c_M\epsilon\le1\), the definition of \(L_M\) implies
\[
 \max\{\lVert M_i\rVert,\lVert\widehat M_i\rVert\}\le L_M.
\]
For \(j\ge1\), the telescoping identity
\[
 \widehat M_i^j-M_i^j
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^{j-1}\widehat M_i^\ell
  (\widehat M_i-M_i)M_i^{j-1-\ell}
\]
therefore gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat M_i^j\widehat d_i-M_i^jd_i\rVert
 &\le \lVert\widehat M_i^j\rVert\lVert\Delta d_i\rVert
 +\lVert\widehat M_i^j-M_i^j\rVert\lVert d_i\rVert\\
 &\le\left(2L_M^j+jL_M^{j-1}c_MD_{\mathrm{norm}}\right)\epsilon.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(j=0\), the same inequality holds with its second summand set to zero.  Bounding the operator norm of a matrix by its Frobenius norm, column by column, and using the definition of \(c_K\), we obtain simultaneously
\[
 \lVert\widehat K_i-K_i\rVert\le c_K\epsilon,
 \qquad i\in\{0,1\}.
\]

On the population cyclic chart, \(K_1=VK_0\) by \(\text{thm:snapshot-frontier}\).  If \(c_K\epsilon\le\kappa/2\), the variational definition of the smallest singular value gives
\[
 \sigma_{\min}(\widehat K_0)
 \ge\sigma_{\min}(K_0)-\lVert\widehat K_0-K_0\rVert
 \ge\kappa/2.
\]
Hence \(\widehat K_0^{-1}\) exists and \(\lVert\widehat K_0^{-1}\rVert\le2/\kappa\).  Using \(K_1=VK_0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}-V
 &=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}-V\widehat K_0\widehat K_0^{-1}\\
 &=(\Delta K_1-V\Delta K_0)\widehat K_0^{-1},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and consequently
\[
 \lVert\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}-V\rVert
 \le\frac{2c_K(1+\lVert V\rVert)}{\kappa}\epsilon
 =c_V\epsilon.
\]
This proves the first assertion under the first three terms in its stated radius.

Now suppose \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\), and abbreviate \(\widehat W=\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\).  The definition of \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) and the preceding inequality imply
\[
 \lVert\widehat W-V\rVert<c_V\epsilon
 <\min\left\{1,\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{stab}}}{2},
                    \frac{\delta_{\log}}2\right\}.
\]
By the definitions of \(\delta_{\mathrm{stab}}\) and \(\delta_{\log}\), it follows that \(\rho(\widehat W)<1\) and \(\operatorname{spec}(\widehat W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing\).  Thus the stable transition and principal-logarithm coordinates are defined.

For every \(A\in\mathbb S^p\), expansion of the two congruences gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V)(A)
 &=-(\widehat W-V)A\widehat W^{\mathsf T}
   -VA(\widehat W-V)^{\mathsf T},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \lVert\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V\rVert_{F\to F}
 \le\lVert\widehat W-V\rVert(\lVert\widehat W\rVert+\lVert V\rVert)
 \le c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\epsilon
 <\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}}{2}.
\]
The last inequality is exactly the final term in \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\).  Since \(\lVert\mathcal L_V^{-1}\rVert_{F\to F}=\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}\), factorization as
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat W}
 =\mathcal L_V\left[I+\mathcal L_V^{-1}
 (\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V)\right]
\]
and the convergent geometric series for the bracketed inverse show that \(\mathcal L_{\widehat W}\) is invertible and
\[
 \lVert\mathcal L_{\widehat W}^{-1}\rVert_{F\to F}
 \le2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}.
\]
Thus every operation in \(\theta(\widehat W,\widehat z)\) is defined: stability also implies \(1\notin\operatorname{spec}(\widehat W)\), so \(I_p-\widehat W\) is invertible.

Subtracting the population and perturbed Stein equations gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat W}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V)
 =\Delta H_0-(\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V)T_V.
\]
Because \(\lVert\Delta H_0\rVert_F\le2\sqrt p\,\epsilon\), the preceding two bounds and the frozen definition of \(c_T\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert
 &\le\lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert_F\\
 &\le2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}
 \left[2\sqrt p+c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\lVert T_V\rVert_F\right]\epsilon\\
 &=c_T\epsilon.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since \(E_V=C_0-T_V\) and \(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat C_0-\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}\),
\[
 \lVert\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}-E_V\rVert
 \le\lVert\Delta C_0\rVert+
      \lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert
 \le(1+c_T)\epsilon=c_E\epsilon.
\]
If \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\), then the two positivity terms in the definition of \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\) and the variational characterization of the least eigenvalue yield
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}})
 \ge t_{\min}-c_T\epsilon>t_{\min}/2>0,
\]
and
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}})
 \ge e_{\min}-c_E\epsilon>e_{\min}/2>0.
\]
Thus all covariance-positivity filters are preserved.

We finally supply the asserted linear bounds for the remaining coordinates.  The closed operator-norm ball of radius \(\delta_{\log}/2\) about \(V\) is a compact subset of the principal-logarithm domain.  On this ball the Fr\'{e}chet derivative of the logarithm has the resolvent representation
\[
 D\operatorname{Log}_U[A]
 =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma
   \log\zeta\,(\zeta I_p-U)^{-1}A(\zeta I_p-U)^{-1}\,d\zeta,
\]
where a finite union of contours \(\Gamma\) in the slit plane can be chosen uniformly around the spectra in the compact ball.  Hence
\[
 L_{\log}:=\frac{\operatorname{length}(\Gamma)}{2\pi}
 \max_{\zeta\in\Gamma}|\log\zeta|
 \sup_U\sup_{\zeta\in\Gamma}
 \lVert(\zeta I_p-U)^{-1}\rVert^2<\infty.
\]
Integrating the derivative along the line segment from \(V\) to \(\widehat W\), which remains in the ball, gives
\[
 \lVert h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(\widehat W)
       -h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(V)\rVert
 \le h^{-1}L_{\log}c_V\epsilon.
\]

Let \(\eta=\lVert(I_p-V)^{-1}\rVert\).  The distance in operator norm from \(I_p-V\) to a singular matrix is \(\sigma_{\min}(I_p-V)=\eta^{-1}\): the lower bound follows from \(\lVert Ax\rVert\ge\sigma_{\min}(A)\lVert x\rVert\), and a rank-one perturbation built from left and right singular vectors attains equality.  Matrices \(U\) with \(I_p-U\) singular satisfy \(\rho(U)\ge1\), so
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{stab}}\le\eta^{-1}.
\]
The reconstruction radius consequently gives
\[
 \eta\lVert\widehat W-V\rVert<\frac12,
 \qquad
 \lVert(I_p-\widehat W)^{-1}\rVert\le2\eta,
\]
where the second inequality follows by factoring \(I_p-\widehat W=(I_p-V)[I_p-(I_p-V)^{-1}(\widehat W-V)]\) and summing the geometric inverse series.

Let \(x^\star=(I_p-V)^{-1}(m_1-Vm_0)\) and let \(\widehat x^\star\) be its perturbed counterpart.  Subtracting the two equilibrium equations gives
\[
 (I_p-\widehat W)(\widehat x^\star-x^\star)
 =\Delta m_1-\widehat W\Delta m_0
   +(\widehat W-V)(x^\star-m_0).
\]
Since \(\lVert\widehat W\rVert\le\lVert V\rVert+1\),
\[
 \lVert\widehat x^\star-x^\star\rVert
 \le2\eta\left[2+\lVert V\rVert
 +c_V(\lVert m_0\rVert+\lVert x^\star\rVert)\right]\epsilon.
\]
Finally, the last coordinate in \(\text{def:parameter-map}\) is the observed initial mean, so
\[
 \lVert\widehat\mu_0-\mu_0\rVert
 =\lVert\widehat m_0-m_0\rVert\le\epsilon.
\]
Together with the transition, Stein, and noise bounds, these estimates establish every asserted coordinatewise conclusion.  The exact raw equations entered only at the population moment vector through \(K_1=VK_0\); no equality of empirical spectra, probe Gram matrices, or empirical raw residuals was assumed.  Therefore the conclusions concern the well-defined reconstruction from perturbed moments and do not claim that \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) obeys the exact population raw equations.

Because \(H_0,H_1\succ0\) by \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\), their symmetric positive-definite square roots and inverse square roots exist.  Define
\[
 a=H_0^{-1/2}d_0,\qquad c=H_1^{-1/2}d_1,
 \qquad U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}.
\]
The inverse change of variables is
\[
 W=H_1^{1/2}UH_0^{-1/2},
\]
so the change is a bijection on \(\mathbb R^{p\times p}\).  Direct multiplication gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1
 &\iff H_1^{-1/2}WH_0W^{\mathsf T}H_1^{-1/2}=I_p\\
 &\iff UU^{\mathsf T}=I_p\\
 &\iff U\in O(p).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For the last equivalence, \(U\) is square, and \(UU^{\mathsf T}=I_p\) makes \(U\) invertible and hence also gives \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_p\).  Likewise,
\[
 Wd_0=d_1
 \iff H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}H_0^{-1/2}d_0=H_1^{-1/2}d_1
 \iff Ua=c.
\]
Thus \(\text{def:three-fiber}\) yields the exact observable representation
\[
 \mathcal F_3\longleftrightarrow\{U\in O(p):Ua=c\}.
\]

If this set is nonempty, orthogonality gives
\[
 \lVert c\rVert_2^2=c^{\mathsf T}c
 =a^{\mathsf T}U^{\mathsf T}Ua
 =a^{\mathsf T}a
 =\lVert a\rVert_2^2,
\]
which proves necessity of the norm equality.  Conversely, suppose \(\lVert a\rVert_2=\lVert c\rVert_2\).  If this common norm is zero, then \(a=c=0\), and every \(U\in O(p)\) is a solution.  If the common norm is positive, extend \(a/\lVert a\rVert_2\) and \(c/\lVert c\rVert_2\) to orthonormal bases of \(\mathbb R^p\).  The linear map sending the first basis to the second is orthogonal and sends \(a\) to \(c\).  This proves sufficiency using only the displayed observable equality.

Fix one solution \(U_0\).  For any other solution \(U\), put \(R_0=U_0^{\mathsf T}U\).  Then
\[
 R_0\in O(p),\qquad R_0a=U_0^{\mathsf T}c=a,
 \qquad U=U_0R_0.
\]
Conversely, every \(R_0\in O(p)\) satisfying \(R_0a=a\) gives the solution \(U_0R_0\), and the representation is unique.  Hence the solution set is a torsor for
\[
 \operatorname{Stab}(a)=\{R_0\in O(p):R_0a=a\}.
\]
If \(a=0\), this stabilizer is \(O(p)\).  If \(a\ne0\), the orthogonal decomposition
\[
 \mathbb R^p=\operatorname{span}(a)\oplus a^\perp
\]
shows that every stabilizer element is the identity on \(\operatorname{span}(a)\) and is an arbitrary orthogonal map on \(a^\perp\); it is therefore isomorphic to \(O(p-1)\).  Since a single nonzero column has rank one, these cases are precisely \(O(p-r)\), where \(r=\operatorname{rank}(a)\in\{0,1\}\).

We derive the dimension rather than assume it.  At \(I_s\), differentiating \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_s\) gives
\[
 Z^{\mathsf T}+Z=0.
\]
A skew-symmetric \(s\times s\) matrix has \(s(s-1)/2\) free entries.  The Cayley formulas
\[
 Z\longmapsto(I_s-Z)(I_s+Z)^{-1},
 \qquad
 Q\longmapsto(I_s-Q)(I_s+Q)^{-1}
\]
are mutually inverse near zero and \(I_s\), respectively; direct transposition verifies that the first image is orthogonal and that the second image is skew-symmetric.  Left translation supplies the same chart at every element of \(O(s)\).  Taking \(s=p-r\) proves
\[
 \dim\mathcal F_3=\dim O(p-r)=\frac{(p-r)(p-r-1)}2.
\]

We next connect this algebraic fiber to structural explanations and justify relative openness.  Let \(W\in\mathcal F_3\) satisfy the three strict filters in the statement.  Since \(\rho(W)<1\), a real Jordan-form bound supplies finite \(A>0\), \(b\in(0,1)\), and \(j_0\) such that \(\lVert W^j\rVert\le Ab^j\) for \(j\ge j_0\).  Therefore
\[
 T_W=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}W^jH_0(W^{\mathsf T})^j
\]
converges, is positive definite because its first summand is \(H_0\succ0\), and satisfies
\[
 T_W-WT_WW^{\mathsf T}=H_0.
\]
It is unique: vectorization of \(D-WDW^{\mathsf T}=0\) gives
\[
 \bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)\operatorname{vec}(D)=0,
\]
and every eigenvalue of \(W\otimes W\) is a product of two eigenvalues of \(W\), so \(\rho(W\otimes W)=\rho(W)^2<1\).  Put
\[
 E'=C_0-T_W\succ0,\qquad \mu'_0=m_0,
 \qquad x'=(I_p-W)^{-1}(m_1-Wm_0).
\]
The last inverse exists because \(\rho(W)<1\) implies \(1\notin\operatorname{spec}(W)\).

The spectral-cut condition defines the real principal logarithm \(G'=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(W)\).  To see the relevant properties directly, on a complex Jordan block \(\lambda I+N\), where \(N^s=0\), the principal logarithm is
\[
 \operatorname{Log}(\lambda I+N)
 =\ell(\lambda)I+
 \sum_{q=1}^{s-1}\frac{(-1)^{q+1}}{q}
 \left(\frac{N}{\lambda}\right)^q,
 \qquad -\pi<\operatorname{Im}\ell(\lambda)<\pi.
\]
Exponentiating this finite nilpotent series returns \(\lambda I+N\).  Conjugate blocks have conjugate logarithms, so the logarithm of the real matrix \(W\) is real.  By \(h>0\) from \(\text{ass:spacing}\), every eigenvalue \(g'\) of \(G'\) satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Re}(g')=h^{-1}\log|\lambda|<0,
 \qquad
 -\frac{\pi}{h}<\operatorname{Im}(g')<\frac{\pi}{h},
\]
using \(|\lambda|<1\).  Thus the reconstructed generator satisfies \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) and \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\).

Construct \(X'_0\sim\mathcal N(m_0,T_W)\), set
\[
 X'_k=W^k(X'_0-x')+x'\qquad(k=0,1,2),
\]
and take mutually independent \(\varepsilon'_k\sim\mathcal N(0,E')\), independently of \(X'_0\).  This obeys \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\), \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\), and \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\).  The definition of \(x'\) gives
\[
 (I_p-W)x'=m_1-Wm_0.
\]
Consequently the first reconstructed mean is \(m_1\), and the probe equation gives the second:
\[
 Wm_1+(I_p-W)x'
 =m_1+W(m_1-m_0)
 =m_1+Wd_0
 =m_1+d_1=m_2.
\]
For covariances, the Stein identity and the congruence in \(\mathcal F_3\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_0)+E'&=T_W+E'=C_0,\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_1)+E'&=WT_WW^{\mathsf T}+E'=C_0-H_0=C_1,\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_2)+E'&=W(T_W-H_0)W^{\mathsf T}+E'\\
 &=T_W-H_0-WH_0W^{\mathsf T}+E'\\
 &=C_0-H_0-H_1=C_2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
All constructed variables are Gaussian, so equality of means and covariances is equality of the three marginal laws.  Conversely, the moment recursions of every structural explanation give \(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1\) and \(Wd_0=d_1\); Hurwitz stability and the alias strip give the first two filters, while uniqueness of the Stein solution gives \(T_W=\Sigma\) and \(C_0-T_W=E\succ0\).  Thus the strict-filter intersection is exactly the admissible transition set for the three observed laws.

The conditions \(\rho(W)<1\) and \(\operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing\) are open in \(W\), by continuity of the roots of the characteristic polynomial.  On the stable set,
\[
 \operatorname{vec}(T_W)
 =\bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)^{-1}\operatorname{vec}(H_0),
\]
which is continuous in \(W\).  Since the least eigenvalue is continuous, \(C_0-T_W\succ0\) is open as well.  The strict-filter intersection is consequently relatively open in the torsor \(\mathcal F_3\), and every nonempty local admissible branch or stratum has the full torsor dimension computed above.

Because \(H_0^{-1/2}\) is invertible, \(d_0\ne0\) is equivalent to \(r=1\), whereas \(d_0=0\) is equivalent to \(r=0\).  In the latter case the norm certificate is equivalent to \(d_1=0\), because \(H_1^{-1/2}\) is invertible.  Hence the local dimension is \((p-1)(p-2)/2>0\) for \(d_0\ne0\) and \(p\ge3\), while it is \(p(p-1)/2>0\) for \(d_0=0\) and \(p\ge2\).  Finally, if a larger unknown-common-measurement-covariance model contains this deterministic Gaussian class and has the same transition target, every pair or continuum of explanations constructed here remains observationally equivalent in that larger class.  Identification in a class implies identification in each of its subclasses; contraposition proves the stated transfer of nonidentification.
